title: Hold-and-wait and the atomic repair
caption: Left: two rigid jobs each holding half their gang, wait arrows closing a cycle, every held GPU idle at full price. Right: atomic gang allocation grants one job everything and queues the other holding nothing, breaking the cycle by construction.

title: The backfill window
caption: A large gang's reservation drains capacity toward its start time. A 128-GPU job with a two-hour estimate fits the idle hole only because its enforced release completes before the reservation needs the GPUs.

title: Scaling efficiency regimes
caption: Efficiency against worker count for the 175B reference job: near-linear while per-worker computation dominates, sublinear as fixed per-step costs surface, saturated when they rival the shrinking computation. Throughput still rises while efficiency falls; the policy window is a choice, not a derivation.

title: Three tiers of use
caption: 500 allocated GPUs narrow to 350 active-equivalents to 280 productive-equivalents. Each gap has a different owner: scheduling losses below allocated, input and runtime losses below active, replay and synchronization below productive.
